name: Tim
title: RT by @tm0klc: “just use a foundation model” they said. so we benchmarked 10 of them against Manako on a real forecourt damage clip. same full 1280x720 frames, same class prompts (person, car, fuel dispenser, fuel nozzle), no crops, no zoom. the hard class is the nozzle/hose. small, thin, occluded, and the thing that actually gets damaged. - Grounding DINO labelled a bin as a fuel nozzle. - Florence-2 labelled the canopy pole as one. - OWL-ViT, YOLOE and YOLO-World got the dispenser at best, never the nozzle. - RF-DETR doesn’t have the class. - Gemma 4 E2B described the scene, boxed the pump, and returned no incident time. the only open model that localised the nozzle was full SAM3. 3.45 GB, 0.2-1 FPS on a Jetson Orin Nano. Manako (3 specialists - 29.5 MB), 3-6 FPS on the same Jetson, tracked the nozzle at 5 FPS and fired a live equipment_damage event on the hose drop at 10.3s. 117x smaller than the only model that could keep up. open-vocab models are great at the classes the internet photographs a lot. operations live in the long tail: nozzles, hoses, cabinets, the small parts that break. that’s where specialised detectors win, and it’s why we built Manako the way we did.

title: RT by @rob_svrn: A credibly neutral network state with its own economy and currency being essential to the proliferation of truly open intelligence is a profound concept. After much study I’ve concluded the same and think that it’s an inevitability. I would **highly** recommend listening to this weeks novelty search where @const_reborn went more in depth on this. He also highlighted what’s coming down the pike next week with updates to Bittensor’s wallet infrastructure in light of the recent AI advancements in mathematics. Bittensor wallets will be able to hide the signing key behind a hash and swap in a new one after every transaction, with post-quantum signatures layered on top, so an elliptic-curve break alone can’t drain them. This highlights a key strength of Bittensor in its current form: being able to quickly upgrade and evolve in a time of great uncertainty improved its anti-fragility. https://youtu.be/F53p-VCto3U?is=kd9P3vue4e22goqr

title: RT by @opentensor: Every company shipping AI agents asks one question: how can I stop my agent from going rogue? To answer it, HaloGuard Output Guard now sets a new state of the art (SOTA): 83.63 average F1, ahead of the previous best at 82.5. All measured on public benchmarks. And we did it with a 0.8B model, a quarter of the size of the previous best. Small enough to run efficiently. Cheap enough to make checking every response practical. This was the focus of Phase 3 on Trishool: • 7,500+ jailbreaks submitted • 125+ unique miners • 15 weeks of challenges It comes at the right time. We’re taking our product to enterprises now, and this makes our security stack stronger. We’ll share the models on Hugging Face, the arXiv paper and a full explainer soon.
